Phở Gà (Chicken Pho)

45 min (mostly hands-off)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Toasted Whole Spices

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, bone-in150g300g450g600g
Water500ml1000ml1500ml2000ml
Yellow onion¼½¾1
Fresh ginger10g20g30g40g
Star anise1234
Whole cloves2468
Coriander seeds¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Cinnamon stick¼½¾1
Fish sauce15ml30ml45ml60ml
Rock sugar5g10g15g20g
Dried flat rice noodles60g120g180g240g
Bean sprouts20g40g60g80g
Thai basil3g6g9g12g
Scallion, sliced5g10g15g20g
Cilantro3g6g9g12g
Lime wedges1234
Red chili, sliced¼½¾1

Steps

  1. Char the onion and ginger over a gas flame or under a broiler until blackened in spots, then rinse off the loose char.
  2. Toast the star anise, cloves, coriander seeds, and cinnamon stick in a dry pot 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
  3. Add the chicken, water, and charred onion and ginger. Bring to a boil, then skim off any foam.
  4. Reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, 30-35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
  5. Lift out the chicken, cool slightly, then shred or slice the meat off the bone.
  6. Strain the broth, discarding the solids, and season with fish sauce and rock sugar to taste.
  7. Soak the rice noodles in hot water 10-15 minutes until softened, then blanch briefly and drain.
  8. Divide the noodles into bowls and top with shredded chicken.
  9. Ladle the hot broth over each bowl.
  10. Top with bean sprouts, Thai basil, scallion, cilantro, chili, and a lime wedge.

Bún Chả (Grilled Pork with Vermicelli & Herbs)

40 min (+30 min marinate)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Pickled Carrot & Daikon (Đồ Chua)

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Ground pork100g200g300g400g
Pork belly or shoulder, thin-sliced60g120g180g240g
Garlic, minced1 clove234
Shallot, minced½11½2
Fish sauce15ml30ml45ml60ml
Sugar5g10g15g20g
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Rice vermicelli60g120g180g240g
Lettuce20g40g60g80g
Mixed herbs (mint, perilla, Thai basil)10g20g30g40g
Pickled carrot & daikon (đồ chua)30g60g90g120g
Nuoc cham (fish sauce, sugar, lime, water, garlic, chili)60ml120ml180ml240ml

Steps

  1. Mix the ground pork with half the garlic, shallot, fish sauce, sugar, and pepper, then shape into small flat patties. Toss the sliced pork belly with the rest.
  2. Cover both and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
  3. Whisk together the nuoc cham: fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, water, minced garlic, and chili.
  4. Julienne the carrot and daikon and toss with a little vinegar, sugar, and salt; let sit 15 minutes to quick-pickle.
  5. Grill or broil the patties and pork belly slices 3-4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
  6. Slide the warm grilled pork into a bowl of the nuoc cham while it's still hot.
  7. Cook the vermicelli noodles according to the package, then rinse under cold water and drain.
  8. Serve the noodles, lettuce, and herbs alongside the bowl of pork in nuoc cham, topped with the pickled carrot and daikon.
  9. Dip noodles and herbs into the sauce bowl bite by bite alongside the pork.

Bánh Mì Thịt Nướng (Grilled Pork Banh Mi)

35 min (+30 min marinate)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Sliced Marinated Pork

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Pork shoulder or loin, thin-sliced120g240g360g480g
Lemongrass, minced1 stalk234
Garlic, minced1234
Shallot, minced½11½2
Fish sauce10ml20ml30ml40ml
Sugar8g16g24g32g
Soy sauce5ml10ml15ml20ml
Sesame oil3ml6ml9ml12ml
Baguette¼½¾1
Pork liver pâté (optional)10g20g30g40g
Mayonnaise10g20g30g40g
Maggi seasoning (or soy sauce)a few drops¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Pickled carrot & daikon (đồ chua)30g60g90g120g
Cucumber, sliced15g30g45g60g
Cilantro3g6g9g12g
Jalapeño or Thai chili¼½¾1

Steps

  1. Combine the pork slices with lemongrass, garlic, shallot, fish sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
  2. Marinate at least 30 minutes (overnight in the fridge tastes best).
  3. Heat a grill pan or broiler until very hot. Cook the pork 2-3 minutes per side until charred and caramelized.
  4. Split the baguette lengthwise and toast lightly.
  5. Spread mayonnaise and pâté inside both halves.
  6. Drizzle a few drops of Maggi seasoning over the bread.
  7. Layer the grilled pork inside.
  8. Top with pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber, cilantro, and sliced chili.
  9. Press the sandwich closed and slice in half to serve.

Bò Lúc Lắc (Shaking Beef)

25 min (+20 min marinate)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Searing Beef with Onion

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Beef sirloin, cubed130g260g390g520g
Soy sauce8ml16ml24ml32ml
Oyster sauce8ml16ml24ml32ml
Fish sauce5ml10ml15ml20ml
Sugar3g6g9g12g
Garlic, minced1234
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Butter5g10g15g20g
Red onion, sliced20g40g60g80g
Watercress (or lettuce)20g40g60g80g
Tomato, sliced¼½¾1
Cucumber, sliced15g30g45g60g
Lime juice (for dipping salt)5ml10ml15ml20ml
Salt & pepper (for dipping)pinchpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp

Steps

  1. Marinate the beef cubes with soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar, garlic, and pepper for 20-30 minutes.
  2. Heat a wok or heavy skillet until very hot with a little oil.
  3. Sear the beef in a single layer, working in batches, 30-45 seconds per side until browned but still pink in the center.
  4. Add the butter and sliced onion, tossing 1-2 minutes until the onion softens and the beef looks glossy.
  5. Arrange the watercress, tomato, and cucumber on a plate.
  6. Pile the beef and onion on top.
  7. Stir the lime juice with a pinch of salt and pepper to make the dipping sauce.
  8. Serve immediately with steamed rice and the lime-salt-pepper dip.

Gỏi Cuốn & Chả Giò (Fresh & Fried Spring Rolls)

45 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Fried Cha Gio

Gỏi Cuốn Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234

Shrimp, cooked & halved lengthwise481216

Chả Giò Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Ground pork60g120g180g240g
Shrimp, chopped30g60g90g120g
Dried wood ear mushroom, soaked & minced5g10g15g20g
Dried glass noodles, soaked & chopped10g20g30g40g
Carrot, grated15g30g45g60g
Jicama (or shredded cabbage)15g30g45g60g
Garlic & shallot, minced½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Egg, beaten (binder)¼½¾1
Fish sauce5ml10ml15ml20ml
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Rice paper or spring roll wrappers2468
Vegetable oil (for frying)100ml200ml300ml400ml
Nuoc cham (for dipping)30ml60ml90ml120ml

Steps

  1. For the chả giò, mix the ground pork, chopped shrimp, wood ear mushroom, glass noodles, carrot, jicama, garlic, shallot, egg, a splash of fish sauce, and a pinch of pepper into a filling.
  2. Spoon filling onto a wrapper, fold in the sides, and roll tightly into a cigar shape; repeat with the remaining wrappers.
  3. Heat the oil to about 170°C (340°F). Fry the rolls in batches 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
  4. Meanwhile for the gỏi cuốn, cook the rice vermicelli according to the package directions and drain.
  5. Dip a rice paper wrapper in warm water 10-15 seconds until just pliable.
  6. Lay lettuce, herbs, vermicelli, and pork belly slices near the bottom edge of the wrapper.
  7. Place the shrimp halves cut-side up just above the filling so they show through the wrapper once rolled.
  8. Fold the bottom of the wrapper over the filling, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly; repeat with the remaining wrappers.
  9. Serve the fresh rolls with peanut hoisin sauce and the fried rolls with nuoc cham.

Gà Kho Gừng (Ginger Caramelized Chicken)

35 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Braising the Chicken

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs or drumsticks, bone-in150g300g450g600g
Fish sauce15ml30ml45ml60ml
Soy sauce5ml10ml15ml20ml
Garlic, minced1234
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Sugar (for caramel)15g30g45g60g
Water (to stop the caramel)15ml30ml45ml60ml
Fresh ginger, julienned15g30g45g60g
Shallots, sliced½11½2
Vegetable oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Scallion, sliced (garnish)3g6g9g12g

Steps

  1. Marinate the chicken with fish sauce, soy sauce, half the garlic, and pepper for 15-20 minutes.
  2. Make the caramel: melt the sugar in a dry pan over medium heat until deep amber, then carefully add the water off the heat to stop it cooking.
  3. Add the oil, remaining garlic, ginger, and shallots to the caramel and stir until fragrant.
  4. Add the marinated chicken and stir to coat evenly; sear 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
  5. Add a splash of water to just cover the bottom of the pan, cover, and simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cooked through.
  6. Uncover and let the sauce reduce 3-5 minutes more, until syrupy and clinging to the chicken.
  7. Garnish with scallion and serve hot with steamed rice.

Canh Chua (Sweet & Sour Fish Soup)

35 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Rice Paddy Herb (Ngò Ôm)

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
White fish steaks (catfish or similar)130g260g390g520g
Tamarind pulp (or paste)15g30g45g60g
Water300ml600ml900ml1200ml
Pineapple, chunked30g60g90g120g
Tomato, wedged½11½2
Okra, sliced2468
Bean sprouts15g30g45g60g
Rice paddy herb (ngò ôm), chopped3g6g9g12g
Fish sauce15ml30ml45ml60ml
Sugar8g16g24g32g
Garlic, minced1234
Fried shallots (garnish)3g6g9g12g
Thai chili, sliced¼½¾1

Steps

  1. Soak the tamarind pulp in a little warm water, mash, and strain to make tamarind water (or dissolve tamarind paste directly).
  2. Sauté the garlic in a splash of oil in a pot until fragrant.
  3. Add the tamarind water and remaining water and bring to a boil.
  4. Season with fish sauce and sugar, tasting until the broth is balanced sour-sweet-salty.
  5. Add the fish steaks and simmer gently 6-8 minutes until just cooked through.
  6. Add the pineapple, tomato, and okra; simmer 3-4 minutes until just tender.
  7. Stir in the bean sprouts and rice paddy herb right at the end so they stay crisp and fragrant.
  8. Ladle into bowls and top with fried shallots and sliced chili.

Bánh Flan (Vietnamese Crème Caramel) (Bonus)

30 min (+4 hr chill)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Custard Ingredients

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Eggs1234
Whole milk80ml160ml240ml320ml
Sugar (for custard)15g30g45g60g
Vanilla extract¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Sugar (for caramel)20g40g60g80g
Water (for caramel)10ml20ml30ml40ml

Steps

  1. Make the caramel: melt the sugar with the water in a small pan over medium heat, swirling until it turns a deep amber.
  2. Immediately pour the hot caramel into ramekins, tilting to coat the bottom, and let it harden.
  3. Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, and vanilla together until just combined, without over-whipping.
  4. Strain the custard through a fine sieve into the caramel-lined ramekins.
  5. Cover with foil, set the ramekins in a baking dish, and pour hot water halfway up their sides.
  6. Bake at 150°C (300°F) for 30-35 minutes, until just set with a slight jiggle in the center.
  7. Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 4 hours.
  8. Run a knife around the edge of each ramekin and invert onto a plate to release the caramel sauce.
